front: What is DNS rebinding in one sentence?
back: One-line: attacker rotates DNS answers to turn the browser into a proxy to internal IPs — bypasses naive same-origin checks — CWE-350.

front: Explain the mental model of DNS rebinding (how the system thinks).
back: Browser loads attacker page from evil.example (legitimate origin at load time). Attacker's DNS TTL is very short; on reconnect the name resolves to 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, or 10.0.0.5. Same-origin policy compares scheme+host+port at request time — if host string still matches but IP is now internal, fetches may hit services that trust "local" clients.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for DNS rebinding?
back: dig suspicious.example A +noall +answer +ttlid → ss -tlnp | grep -E ':(6379|11211|8080|9200)\s' → curl -s --max-time 2 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/

front: Given a broken DNS rebinding setup, what is your first validation command?
back: dig suspicious.example A +noall +answer +ttlid

front: What are the production-safe defaults for DNS rebinding?
back: 1. Bind services to specific interfaces

front: Symptom: Internal API hit from "external" referer — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Access logs show Host=public name, src=127.0.0.1 · Fix: Host allowlist; bind service to internal IP only

front: Symptom: Metadata stolen from browser chain — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: IMDS hop limit, metadata service v2 · Fix: AWS IMDSv2 required + hop limit 1; firewall 169.254.169.254 from containers

front: Symptom: Redis/Mongo "random" commands — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: MONITOR; bind address · Fix: bind 127.0.0.1; require AUTH; SG restrict port

front: Symptom: Dev laptop compromised via local service — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: ss -tlnp for 0.0.0.0 listeners · Fix: Bind localhost; use firewall (ufw) default deny

front: Symptom: Pen test flags DNS rebinding — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: PoC resolves to internal IP · Fix: Implement mitigations above; document accepted risk only with auth layer

front: Gotcha with DNS rebinding: what silently fails?
back: 0.0.0.0 bind on a laptop behind a browser = rebinding target. "It's dev only" doesn't matter if you visit the internet on the same machine.

front: When should you NOT use DNS rebinding?
back: Offensive testing without written scope — rebinding against third parties is illegal. Assuming CORS (Cross Origin Request Sharing) alone fixes this — CORS governs cross-origin reads, not DNS-to-IP mapping attacks on same host string.

front: What is DNS zone in one sentence?
back: One-line: a contiguous DNS namespace slice served authoritatively by one or more NS — RFC 1035.

front: Explain the mental model of DNS zone (how the system thinks).
back: A zone is everything below a zone apex (e.g. example.com) that one administrative entity controls. The parent zone (.com) holds NS glue pointing to your nameservers.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for DNS zone?
back: .com (parent zone) → dig @ns1.example.com example.com AXFR # zone transfer (often ACL'd) → dig @ns1.example.com example.com SOA +short → dig @ns1.example.com example.com NS +short → for ns in ns1 ns2; do

front: Given a broken DNS zone setup, what is your first validation command?
back: .com (parent zone)

front: Symptom: Some resolvers get old IP — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SOA serial on all NS; TTL remaining · Fix: Bump serial; ensure secondaries synced (rndc notify / provider auto-sync)

front: Symptom: Zone transfer fails — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: dig AXFR @primary; firewall TCP/53 · Fix: ACL on primary; allow secondary IP; check TSIG key

front: Symptom: Subdomain NXDOMAIN — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Delegation NS in parent vs child zone · Fix: Add NS + glue at parent OR record in parent zone — not both incorrectly

front: Symptom: Apex MX/TXT broken after adding CNAME — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CNAME coexists with nothing else at apex · Fix: Remove apex CNAME; use ALIAS or separate name

front: Symptom: DNSSEC validation fails — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: dig +dnssec; DS at parent matches DNSKEY · Fix: Re-sign zone; publish correct DS to registrar

front: Symptom: Serial not incrementing — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Secondary serving stale data · Fix: Always increment SOA serial on change (automate in CI)

front: Symptom: Wildcard surprises — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: *.example.com catches unintended names · Fix: Narrow wildcard; explicit records override wildcard

front: Gotcha with DNS zone: what silently fails?
back: Forgot to bump SOA serial → secondaries never pick up changes. Automate serial in dynamic DNS or use provider-managed zones.

front: When should you NOT use DNS zone?
back: Single static host entry on one machine → /etc/hosts or local dnsmasq stub. Global anycast without understanding secondary sync → managed DNS (Route53, Cloudflare) reduces ops load.

front: What is DNS in one sentence?
back: One-line: distributed naming that maps names → records (A, AAAA, CNAME, …) via a resolver chain — Kleppmann, DDIA + RFC 1035.

front: Explain the mental model of DNS (how the system thinks).
back: DNS is a hierarchical, cached lookup system. Your stub resolver doesn't talk to root directly for every query — it follows referrals or uses a recursive resolver (ISP, 8.8.8.8, corporate Unbound).

back: /etc/resolv.conf minimal:

front: Symptom: NXDOMAIN everywhere for one name — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: dig +trace stops where? · Fix: Fix NS delegation or missing zone at authoritative

front: Symptom: Works with @8.8.8.8, fails with corporate DNS — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Compare dig @corp-dns vs public · Fix: Internal split-horizon; add private zone or conditional forwarder

front: Symptom: Intermittent wrong IP — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: TTL + multiple A records; geo DNS · Fix: Lower TTL during migration; verify all authoritative NS agree (dig @each-ns)

front: Symptom: Slow first query, fast after — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: dig twice; check +stats query time · Fix: Resolver cold cache normal; fix upstream if always slow

front: Symptom: SERVFAIL — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: dig +dnssec; check authoritative logs · Fix: Broken DNSSEC chain; DS/DNSKEY mismatch

front: Symptom: Large response fails — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: dig +ignore vs +bufsize=512 shows TC bit · Fix: Enable EDNS0 or TCP on resolver/firewall

front: Symptom: Pod resolves, host doesn't (or reverse) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: resolvectl; CoreDNS vs host resolv · Fix: K8s ndots / search suffix issue — use FQDN with trailing dot

front: Symptom: After zone cutover, stale answers — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: TTL on old records (300–86400 common) · Fix: Wait TTL or flush resolver cache; don't assume instant global update

front: Gotcha with DNS: what silently fails?
back: search domain suffix causes surprise lookups. curl api may query api.ec2.internal before api — always use FQDN (api.example.com.) in automation.

front: When should you NOT use DNS?
back: Service-to-service naming inside a cluster → platform DNS (K8s, Consul) is faster to iterate. Storing non-DNS data in TXT beyond reasonable size — use a real config store.

front: What is Cloudflare in one sentence?
back: Authoritative DNS + reverse proxy (orange cloud) + WAF/CDN/DDoS — changes where traffic terminates and who sees origin IP. Cloudflare docs + migration incidents when proxy hid real client IP or broke TLS.

front: Explain the mental model of Cloudflare (how the system thinks).
back: Cloudflare sits between users and origin: as DNS provider (nameservers → Cloudflare) and optionally HTTP proxy (proxied records). Proxied traffic: client → Cloudflare edge → your origin. OID identifies objects in Cloudflare API (zones, records, rulesets).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Cloudflare?
back: User ──► CF edge (TLS, cache, WAF) ──► origin (ALB, nginx, Vercel) → App logs: use CF-Connecting-IP, not $remote_addr (which is CF edge).

front: Given a broken Cloudflare setup, what is your first validation command?
back: User ──► CF edge (TLS, cache, WAF) ──► origin (ALB, nginx, Vercel)

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Cloudflare?
back: 1. Add site in Cloudflare dashboard → import/copy DNS records. 2. Change registrar NS to Cloudflare-assigned nameservers. 3. Choose proxied vs DNS-only per record (A/AAAA/CNAME).

front: Symptom: Too many redirects — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: SSL mode vs origin HTTP/HTTPS · Fix: Full (strict) + HTTPS origin; or fix origin redirect loop

front: Symptom: 522 / 523 connection to origin — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Origin down; SG/firewall blocks CF IPs · Fix: Open firewall to CF IP ranges; health check origin

front: Symptom: 525 SSL handshake failed — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Origin cert expired/wrong name · Fix: Renew cert; match hostname

front: Symptom: Wrong client IP in logs — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Not reading CF header · Fix: CF-Connecting-IP / True-Client-IP (Enterprise)

front: Symptom: API CORS breaks after CF — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Transform rules; cached OPTIONS · Fix: Bypass cache; preserve headers (CORS (Cross Origin Request Sharing))

front: Symptom: DNS propagates but site wrong — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Orange vs grey cloud; old A record · Fix: Toggle proxy; purge DNS cache

front: Symptom: Webhook HMAC fail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Body buffered/transformed · Fix: Disable buffering on webhook path

front: Gotcha with Cloudflare: what silently fails?
back: Flexible SSL — users see HTTPS, CF→origin may be plain HTTP. Compliance fail and session hijack on that leg.

front: When should you NOT use Cloudflare?
back: Internal-only services — no public DNS/proxy needed; use private DNS (Route53 private zone, mDNS). WebSockets/long polling without config — works on CF but verify timeout/cache rules. Replacing WAF on complex custom protocols — CF is HTTP-centric; raw TCP needs Spectrum (paid).

front: What is DNS record in one sentence?
back: Name → type → value mapping in a zone — A/AAAA/CNAME/TXT/MX with TTL controlling cache stickiness.

front: Explain the mental model of DNS record (how the system thinks).
back: Resolvers cache answers per TTL (seconds). Lower TTL before changes = faster global cutover. CNAME can't apex @ on all providers (use ALIAS/ANAME at Route53/Cloudflare). TXT for SPF/DKIM/verification. Propagation = old TTL expiring everywhere, not instant magic.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for DNS record?
back: Client → recursive resolver (cache TTL) → authoritative NS → zone file/RRset → dig yourdomain.com A +short → dig www.yourdomain.com CNAME → dig yourdomain.com TXT → dig yourdomain.com NS

front: Given a broken DNS record setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Client → recursive resolver (cache TTL) → authoritative NS → zone file/RRset

front: What are the production-safe defaults for DNS record?
back: 1. Note current TTL (dig yourdomain.com A → ANSWER TTL) 2. Lower TTL to 300 (5 min); wait old TTL to expire 3. Change A/CNAME/TXT 4. Verify with multiple resolvers 5. Raise TTL again (3600+) when stable

front: Symptom: Old IP still resolves — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: TTL cache · Fix: Wait TTL; dig @1.1.1.1 vs local

front: Symptom: Apex CNAME rejected — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Provider rules · Fix: ALIAS record or A to load balancer

front: Symptom: Cert validation fails — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: _acme-challenge TXT · Fix: Add exact token; no extra quotes

front: Symptom: Email bounces — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: MX + SPF TXT · Fix: MX points to mail host; SPF includes sender

front: Symptom: Subdomain wrong zone — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: NS delegation · Fix: Child zone NS at parent

front: Symptom: Intermittent answers — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Split DNS · Fix: Internal vs public view mismatch

front: Gotcha with DNS record: what silently fails?
back: CNAME at www only, apex A/ALIAS — classic migration mistake. Trailing dot — FQDN in some UIs needs @ or full stop semantics. **Wildcard * doesn't cover nested** — *.example.com ≠ a.b.example.com on all setups.

front: When should you NOT use DNS record?
back: Don't set TTL 0 in production — resolver load + instability. Don't chain CNAME → CNAME → … — flatten or use ALIAS.

front: What is mDNS in one sentence?
back: One-line: link-local multicast DNS for .local names without a central server — RFC 6762 (Bonjour / Avahi).

front: Explain the mental model of mDNS (how the system thinks).
back: mDNS (multicast DNS) resolves hostnames on a local link via UDP 5353 to 224.0.0.251 (IPv4) / ff02::fb (IPv6). Queries and responses are multicast — any host on the segment can answer for names it owns.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for mDNS?
back: Laptop LAN (same broadcast domain) → systemctl status avahi-daemon → avahi-browse -a -r # browse all services on LAN → avahi-resolve -n myhost.local → resolvectl status # look for "MulticastDNS setting"

front: Given a broken mDNS setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Laptop LAN (same broadcast domain)

front: What are the production-safe defaults for mDNS?
back: Disable mDNS on servers that shouldn't advertise (security hardening):

front: Symptom: *.local doesn't resolve — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: avahi-daemon running? VLAN isolation? · Fix: Enable mDNS on interface; ensure same L2 segment (no mDNS across routed VLANs without reflector)

front: Symptom: Works on Wi-Fi, not Ethernet — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Different VLANs / AP client isolation · Fix: Move to same broadcast domain or deploy mDNS gateway/reflector (e.g. Avahi reflector, UniFi mDNS)

front: Symptom: Duplicate name conflicts — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: avahi-browse -a shows multiple same names · Fix: Rename host; Avahi appends -2 suffix on conflict

front: Symptom: Chromecast / printer not found — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Multicast blocked on AP/guest network · Fix: Disable guest isolation; allow UDP/5353 between IoT VLAN and client VLAN via reflector

front: Symptom: K8s pod needs .local — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Pods aren't on LAN · Fix: Use cluster DNS (CoreDNS), not mDNS

front: Symptom: High multicast noise — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Many devices advertising · Fix: Reduce advertised services; disable on headless servers

front: Gotcha with mDNS: what silently fails?
back: mDNS crosses trust boundaries poorly. A compromised LAN device can spoof printer.local or _ssh._tcp.local. Never treat mDNS answers as authenticated.

front: When should you NOT use mDNS?
back: Production service discovery across datacenters → use Consul, etcd, or K8s DNS. Anything requiring authoritative global naming → use unicast DNS. Security-sensitive authentication endpoints → never rely on mDNS for identity.

front: What is Top-Level Domain (TLD) in one sentence?
back: Rightmost DNS label in a name (example.com → TLD is com) — delegated by root, operated by registry, sold by registrars. Matters for DNSSEC, resolver behavior, and policy (who can register what).

front: What is .dev?
back: HSTS preload eligible (HTTPS-only expectation).

front: What is .app?
back: similar HTTPS-leaning policies on some resolvers.

front: What is Brand TLD?
back: marketing; same DNS mechanics, higher cost.

front: Explain the mental model of Top-Level Domain (TLD) (how the system thinks).
back: The DNS tree is hierarchical: root (.) → TLD (.com, .org, .uk) → SLD (example in example.com) → subdomains (www). ICANN policy; registry runs TLD nameservers; registrar (GoDaddy, Route53 Registrar) is where you pay and set delegation NS.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Top-Level Domain (TLD)?
back: . (root) ──► .com (TLD) ──► example.com (registered zone) ──► www.example.com → dig +trace example.com A → whois example.com | grep -i 'Name Server\|Registrar'

front: Symptom: Domain "not found" / NXDOMAIN — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Partial global resolution — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: com works, co.uk cookie weird — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Public suffix rules · Fix: Set Domain= cookie per eTLD+1 rules

front: Symptom: DNSSEC SERVFAIL — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: DS record at registrar stale · Fix: Update DS after KSK rollover

front: Symptom: Email SPF/DMARC fail on new TLD — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: No MX/TXT at delegation · Fix: Add records at authoritative zone

front: Symptom: Internal "TLD" collision — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Using .local / .corp on internet · Fix: Use .internal (RFC 6762 guidance) or subdomain under owned domain

front: Gotcha with Top-Level Domain (TLD): what silently fails?
back: Registrar ≠ DNS host — expiry at registrar kills delegation even if Route53 zone exists.

front: When should you NOT use Top-Level Domain (TLD)?
back: Debating TLD for infra — pick one registered domain; use subdomains for envs (staging.example.com). Deep TLD policy research in ops runbooks — registrar support for disputes; ops cares about NS and TTL.

back: Referencing an unset shell variable is an error when set -u (nounset) is on — catches typos before prod scripts half-run.

front: Explain the mental model of Unbound variable (bash set -u) (how the system thinks).
back: Default bash expands unset vars to empty string — silent bugs (rm -rf $DIR/ with empty DIR). set -u (or set -o nounset) aborts on unbound expansion. Often paired with set -e (errexit) and set -o pipefail in strict scripts. Not the Unbound DNS resolver — that's DNS infrastructure software.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Unbound variable (bash set -u)?
back: set -euo pipefail → IFS=$'\n\t' → PORT="${PORT:-8080}" # default if unset → echo "${myvar:-fallback}" → if -v myvar ; then

front: Given a broken Unbound variable (bash set -u) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: set -euo pipefail

front: Symptom: unbound variable on start — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Line number in trace · Fix: set -x; assign var or use ${var:-}

front: Symptom: Works interactively, fails in CI — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CI omits env · Fix: Export required env in workflow

front: Symptom: $1 empty in script — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: No args passed · Fix: :${1:?usage: $0 file}

front: Symptom: Array unset — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: set -u + empty array · Fix: "${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}" pattern

front: Symptom: Sourced script order — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Parent set -u · Fix: Initialize before source

front: Gotcha with Unbound variable (bash set -u): what silently fails?
back: $? immediately after — test commands carefully with set -e. read var without default — can trip nounset on empty input in loops. Don't confuse with Unbound DNS — resolver config is /etc/unbound/unbound.conf.

front: When should you NOT use Unbound variable (bash set -u)?
back: Don't enable set -u in ad-hoc interactive shells unless you enjoy surprise exits. Don't use empty default :- to hide missing required config — fail loud with :? for secrets/paths.

front: Design a minimal correct Unbound variable (bash set -u) setup for a small production service.
back: Checklist: (1) mental-model constraint, (2) required config/commands, (3) health/triage check, (4) one failure mode to avoid. Anchor: set -euo pipefail
